internet-gateway.label: Internet Gateway
internet-gateway.placement: The Internet Gateway sits on the VPC border, at the bottom of the low band: it is the gate between the ground and your sky.

nat-gateway.label: NAT Gateway
nat-gateway.placement: A NAT Gateway lives in the low band, in a public subnet. It needs the Internet Gateway to do its job.

load-balancer.label: Application Load Balancer
load-balancer.placement: The load balancer lives in the low band and stretches across both Availability Zones. It is the one cloud kite strings are meant to reach.

ec2-instance.label: EC2 instance
ec2-instance.placement: Instances live in the mid band, in private subnets, where kite strings cannot reach them directly. A bastion host is the exception: it has a public address, so it goes in a public subnet in the low band.

s3-bucket.label: S3 bucket
s3-bucket.placement: S3 stands outside the VPC and spans every altitude: it is a regional service, not something inside a subnet.

iam-role.label: IAM role
iam-role.placement: IAM lives in the high band, with the things that belong to your AWS account rather than to any one network. Its threads reach down to whatever wears the role.

auto-scaling-group.label: Auto Scaling group
auto-scaling-group.placement: A fleet of instances lives where instances live: the mid band, in private subnets, spread across both Availability Zones.

waf-web-acl.label: WAF web ACL
waf-web-acl.placement: A web ACL hangs beneath the load balancer it protects, like a net: drop it in the low band, and it is associated with the load balancer there.

kms-key.label: KMS key
kms-key.placement: A KMS key lives in the high band with the other managed services, outside the VPC. On its own it protects nothing: choose it in a bucket's default encryption, or for a database's encrypted copy.

session-manager.label: Session Manager
session-manager.placement: Session Manager lives in the high band with the other managed services, outside the VPC. It reaches managed instances over a connection their own SSM Agent opens, so nothing has to open an inbound port.
